A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable text, equations, four figures, three tables, and complete reference lists. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 presents a literature survey and taxonomy. Its empirical observations, including the analyses in Section 7, are attributed to earlier studies rather than experiments or data analysis conducted for this survey.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. Added comparisons and descriptions of recent studies do not report original experimental or data-analysis results produced by this work.

M1.justification: The survey's VP/VPT framework and algorithmic formulations in Sections 2.1–2.4 remain unchanged. Newly discussed methods belong to cited work; no original algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. Expanded discussion of existing application domains and additional literature does not introduce datasets or tasks actually evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Changes to the method inventories in Tables 1–3 concern surveyed literature, not comparator membership in an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is introduced or revised. The existing descriptions of cited evaluations remain stable; new recommendations about model access, adaptation depth, and memory constraints are guidance rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 7 retains the cited attention, NMI, transfer, prompt-placement, and prompt-length analyses. The added mechanism comparisons and domain summaries are interpretive synthesis, not new ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version adds run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The existing discussion of initialization-dependent training variance in Section 8 is retained.

E6.justification: Sections 5.2.1 and 5.3.1 newly summarize qualitative outcomes from cited work: reduced API costs for prime-then-reprogram and improved stability/efficiency for surrogate-based black-box adaptation. No benchmark scores are added, and Section 7's existing empirical findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, including the adaptation objectives, NMI expression, and attention-rank argument, are retained. New prose about comparative capabilities and theoretical ceilings introduces no formal definition, theorem, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a comprehensive, unified survey distinguishing pixel-level VP from internal VPT and classifying prompt-generation mechanisms. The abstract clarifies this existing taxonomy; the introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution and novelty claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds Section 2.5 comparing fixed, learnable, and generated prompts, explanatory selection rationales across Sections 4.1–4.8, and a three-scenario decision guide in Section 8. These substantially expand applicability boundaries, mechanism explanations, and trade-offs involving access, domain shift, memory, and latency.

D1.justification: The documented companion-resource access point changes from a GitHub repository linked in the abstract to a GitHub Pages project site on the title page. No new experimental implementation details or reproduction instructions are disclosed.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on clinical AI-expert feedback, local/surrogate black-box adaptation, and PAE in Table 1. Other references, including AutoPrompt, CoDA, and TC-CLIP, are removed. These update the surveyed literature without substantially changing the survey's vision-focused positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract clarifies terminology, Section 2.5 and the Section 8 selection guide add local structure, and front matter and bibliography entries are revised. Most existing prose and the overall nine-section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The four figures and table designs are retained. Table 1 adds PAE and removes Fg-VP and AutoPrompt; Tables 2–3 also lose selected rows and move within the document. Publication headers and an expanded author page alter layout, with the abstract moving to page 2.

improvement.justification: V2 provides more practical comparative synthesis in Sections 2.5, 4, and 8. However, Section 2.5 newly calls fixed prompts the only viable black-box option, contradicting the retained BlackVIP discussion in Sections 2.2 and 5.3.1. Descriptions such as CoDA and TC-CLIP also remain after their source citations are removed. Added guidance therefore coexists with consistency and traceability losses, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
